decks.name: LeetCode #17 - Letter Combinations of a Phone Number
decks.description: Generate all possible letter combinations from phone number digits using backtracking

cards.question: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number: Given a string containing digits from 2-9 inclusive, return all possible letter combinations that the number could represent. Return the answer in any order. A mapping of digits to letters (just like on the telephone buttons) is given below. Note that 1 does not map to any letters.

solutions.name: Backtracking
solutions.explanation: Use recursive backtracking to generate all letter combinations. Create mapping from digits to their corresponding letters. Start with empty string and current digit index. Base case when current string length equals digits length, add to result. For each character mapped to current digit, recursively build combination with next digit and character appended. Explores all possible combinations systematically. O(n*4^n) time where n is digits length, 4 is max letters per digit. Generates all combinations through exhaustive search.

solutions.timeDescription: Generate all possible combinations where n is number of digits, each digit has up to 4 letters (7 and 9), each combination takes O(n) to build
solutions.spaceDescription: Recursion stack depth O(n) for n digits, output stores all combinations with average length n
solutions.exampleWalkthrough: Given digits='23': Map 2→abc, 3→def. Start backtrack(0,''). Try 'a': backtrack(1,'a'). Try 'd': 'ad' complete, add to res. Try 'e': 'ae' complete. Try 'f': 'af' complete. Backtrack to 'b': backtrack(1,'b'). Generate 'bd','be','bf'. Backtrack to 'c': generate 'cd','ce','cf'. Result: ['ad','ae','af','bd','be','bf','cd','ce','cf'] with 3*3=9 combinations.

solutions.name: Iteration
solutions.explanation: Build letter combinations iteratively without recursion. Start with list containing empty string. For each digit in input, create temporary list for new combinations. For each existing string in result, append each letter mapped to current digit, add to temporary list. Replace result with temporary list. Iteratively builds combinations level by level. More memory intensive as stores all intermediate results but no recursion overhead. Same O(n*4^n) time complexity. Good for avoiding stack overflow on very long input.

solutions.spaceDescription: Temporary list stores intermediate results up to size of output, no recursion stack needed, output stores all combinations
solutions.exampleWalkthrough: Given digits='23': Map 2→abc, 3→def. Start res=['']. Process digit '2': For '', append a/b/c. tmp=['a','b','c'], res=['a','b','c']. Process digit '3': For 'a', append d/e/f to get 'ad','ae','af'. For 'b', append d/e/f to get 'bd','be','bf'. For 'c', append d/e/f to get 'cd','ce','cf'. tmp=['ad','ae','af','bd','be','bf','cd','ce','cf'], res=tmp. Return 9 combinations.
